messages.subject: ggplot2 line graph - scaled?
parts:
I am having trouble telling ggplot2 to graph this dataset [1]. The
resulting plot [2] is nothing compared to what I get [3] when I use R
base graphics.

I suspect ggplot2 is automatically scaling the data; how do I go about
getting the results I get when I use base graphics?

ggplot2 code

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 line graph - scaled?
parts:
On Tue, Dec 11, 2012 at 1:59 PM, Lighton Phiri <lighto...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Neat! Exactly what I wanted --thank you very much Adam. I am curious as to
> why ggplot2 behaves like it did by default though...

ggplot2 is not doing anything unusual. You mapped a numeric vector on
the x axis, and did not change the default x-axis scale, so you got a
plot where the x-axis intervals map to the numeric difference between
each successive x-axis value. If that's not what you want you can
change it--either by telling ggplot to ignore the numeric values of
Workload (as Adam suggested) or by using a log scale (as baptiste
suggested)--but it is the reasonable default.

Best,
Ista
